The actual $C^2$ potential suffices for the following direct calculation. In Cartesian Minkowski coordinates the connection coefficients vanish; by [F1], the supplied $C^2$ curve obeys the Lorentz law, whose lowered time component is $m\,dU_0/d\tau=qF_{0i}U^i$. Since $A_0=-\phi/c$, $A_i=0$ and $\partial_0\phi=0$, exterior differentiation gives $F_{0i}=-\partial_iA_0=\partial_i\phi/c$. The chain rule therefore yields $dC/d\tau=qF_{0i}U^i+q\partial_iA_0U^i=0$ at every interior parameter value. A real differentiable function with zero derivative is constant on each compact interior subinterval by the mean-value theorem; continuity extends the same value to the included endpoints of the finite segment. This proves constancy at the stated $C^2$ regularity without a smooth-potential application of [F2]. [given, F1, F2, A1, algebra]

actual_relevant_use_quotes.3.1: For an explicit work check, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $A_0=-\phi/c$ give $\mathbf E=-\nabla\phi$ and $\mathbf B=0$, so the flat Lorentz law is $d(\gamma m\mathbf w)/dt=q\mathbf E$. Thus $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=q\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf w$, whereas $d(q\phi)/dt=q\nabla\phi\cdot\mathbf w=-q\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf w$. The two work terms cancel, agreeing with step 2.1. [F1, A1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
